title: `+ - * /` on DOUBLE and FLOAT round once
verdict: correctly rounded (≤ 0.5 ulp) in each type, also a division by a literal
description: `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` on DOUBLE are the C++ operators on `double`, on FLOAT the operators on `float`: one IEEE operation, rounded once to nearest, ties to even, in the operands' own type. A FLOAT operation stays in binary32 and returns FLOAT. A division by a literal is the same division.

Bounds in ulps of the result type: add, sub, mul, div ≤ 0.5 for fp64 and fp32 (correctly rounded); `x / c` for a literal `c` ≤ 0.5. Observed on macOS arm64, 3 000 inputs each: max 0.5000 and 0 results off the correctly rounded value, for every operation and type. These are hardware operations, so the bound holds on every platform; the Linux run should give the same.
reference: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply` and `divide` on doubles round once, `rounding: TIE_TO_EVEN` (Lean's native `Float`). sverify's ε for them is 0.5 ulp (#85).

evidence.note: AddOperator: `left + right` on float and on double
DivideOperator: `left / right` on float and on double

evidence.sql: SELECT a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b FROM t  -- t(a DOUBLE, b DOUBLE), 3 000 rows: random signs and exponents in [-60, 60], every fifth pair nearly equal
evidence.observed: max 0.5000, 0.5000, 0.4994, 0.4999 ulp; 0 of 3 000 off the correctly rounded value for each

evidence.sql: SELECT a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b FROM t  -- t(a FLOAT, b FLOAT), the same pairs rounded to binary32
evidence.observed: max 0.5000, 0.5000, 0.5000, 0.5000 ulp of binary32; 0 of 3 000 off; result type FLOAT

evidence.sql: SELECT a / CAST(c AS DOUBLE) FROM t  -- c in 49, 3, 10, 0.1, 7.3; also with FLOAT

provenance.notes: Probe script ulp_probe.py (session scratchpad, not in the repository), run from python/ as `uv run --with mpmath python ulp_probe.py --n 3000 --seed 1 --out ulp.json`: about 3 000 inputs per operation and type, random and hard cases, against mpmath at 256 bits. 'bad' counts results that differ from the correctly rounded value; the max is in ulps of the result type at the exact value's binade. DuckDB runs on a table loaded from Parquet, Polars on a LazyFrame with collect(engine='streaming'), so the column kernels run. DuckDB 2.0.0 and Polars 2.1.0 (Python wheels), macOS 26.6 arm64, Python 3.12.11, mpmath 1.3.0.
